I need to correct my understanding of the function names in this kernel tree — the runtime suspend callback is actually `intel_runtime_suspend` rather than `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`, and the display suspend function has been renamed to `intel_display_driver_suspend`. Now I'm gathering the line numbers to construct an accurate trace.
## Findings first: two of the three named symbols don't exist in this tree

I grepped the whole tree (kernel v7.0.0-rc, `/workspace/linux`):

| Symbol you named | Status |
|---|---|
| `i915_pm_suspend` | exists — `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1392` |
| `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` | **does not exist anywhere** (`rg` returns no hits). The runtime-PM callback is named `intel_runtime_suspend` (`i915_driver.c:1545`) |
| `intel_display_suspend` | **does not exist anywhere.** It was renamed; the equivalent is `intel_display_driver_suspend` (`display/intel_display_driver.c:684`) |

So the "list which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`" part has an empty answer as literally asked — and it is empty for a structural reason, not just a naming one (see §2). I answered against the real symbols below.

## 1. Every PCI PM callback reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

`i915_pm_suspend` is only ever installed as a callback pointer; nothing in the driver calls it by name. It is reached from exactly two slots in `i915_pm_ops` (`i915_driver.c:1713`), which is hooked up at `i915_pci.c:1031` (`.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops`):

```
pci_driver i915_pci_driver.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops   (i915_pci.c:1031)
  ├─ .suspend  = i915_pm_suspend    (i915_driver.c:1719)   [PMSG_SUSPEND / S3, S0ix]
  └─ .poweroff = i915_pm_suspend    (i915_driver.c:1745)   [PMSG_HIBERNATE / S4]
```

Both entries are the *same function*, so there is one call chain body with two entry events:

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)                 i915_driver.c:1392
  ├─ kdev_to_i915(kdev)                              i915_drv.h:328
  ├─ guard: !i915                       -> -ENODEV
  ├─ guard: switch_power_state == DRM_SWITCH_POWER_OFF -> 0   (early out, no display work)
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                    i915_driver.c:1103
```

A third, non-`dev_pm_ops` path reaches the same `i915_drm_suspend` without going through `i915_pm_suspend`:

```
vga_switcheroo_client_ops.set_gpu_state = i915_switcheroo_set_state   i915_switcheroo.c:62,16
  └─ i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo(i915, pmm)                        i915_driver.c:1207
       ├─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                                i915_driver.c:1223
       └─ i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)                    i915_driver.c:1227
```

And `.freeze` reaches `i915_drm_suspend` directly too, bypassing `i915_pm_suspend`:

```
.freeze = i915_pm_freeze   (i915_driver.c:1741, defined :1487)
  └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)   i915_driver.c:1493   + i915_gem_freeze()
```

Full set of `dev_pm_ops` suspend-side siblings, for context (none of these reach `i915_pm_suspend`):
`.prepare`→`i915_pm_prepare`, `.suspend_late`→`i915_pm_suspend_late`→`i915_drm_suspend_late(.., false)`, `.suspend_noirq`→`i915_pm_suspend_noirq`, `.freeze_late`→`i915_pm_freeze_late`→`i915_drm_suspend_late(.., true)`, `.poweroff_late`→`i915_pm_poweroff_late`→`i915_drm_suspend_late(.., true)`, `.poweroff_noirq`→`i915_pm_poweroff_noirq`.

## 2. Which of those callers also call the runtime-suspend path

**None — and they cannot.** `intel_runtime_suspend` is installed only as `.runtime_suspend` (`i915_driver.c:1752`) and is never called by name from any system-suspend callback. The two families are disjoint by design:

- System suspend: `i915_pm_suspend` → `i915_drm_suspend` → display teardown via `intel_display_driver_suspend`
- Runtime suspend: `intel_runtime_suspend` (`:1545`) → `i915_gem_runtime_suspend`, `intel_gt_runtime_suspend`, `intel_display_power_suspend` — **no** `intel_display_driver_suspend` call at all

They only *converge* on shared leaf helpers, which is the real overlap worth naming:

| leaf helper | `i915_drm_suspend[_late]` | `intel_runtime_suspend` |
|---|---|---|
| `intel_irq_suspend` | ✔ (`:1122`) | ✔ (`:1573`) |
| `intel_uncore_suspend` | ✔ (`:1168`, per-gt) | ✔ (`:1576`, per-gt) |
| `vlv_suspend_complete` | ✔ (`:1172`) | ✔ (`:1580`) |
| `intel_runtime_pm_driver_release` | ✔ (`:1183`) | ✔ (`:1597`) |
| `intel_display_power_suspend_late` / `_suspend` | `_late(display, s2idle)` | `_suspend(display)` |

## 3. `dev_priv` data flow: `i915_drm_suspend` → `intel_display_driver_suspend`

The key point: **`dev_priv` is not passed down.** It is converted to an `intel_display *` one level up and only that opaque pointer crosses the boundary.

```
i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  kdev  ──dev_get_drvdata──▶ drm_device*  ──container_of──▶ drm_i915_private* i915
                                          (kdev_to_i915, i915_drv.h:328-333)
  │
  │ passes &i915->drm  (back to a drm_device*, not dev_priv)
  ▼
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)                       i915_driver.c:1103
  dev_priv = to_i915(dev);                                     :1105  (container_of, i915_drv.h:323)
  display  = dev_priv->display;                                :1106  (field, i915_drv.h:172)
  │
  ├─ dev_priv used locally only, for non-display state:
  │    &dev_priv->runtime_pm      -> disable/enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts   :1108, :1141
  │    to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt      -> i915_ggtt_suspend                   :1134
  │    suspend_to_idle(dev_priv)  -> picks PCI_D1 vs PCI_D3cold          :1136
  │    dev_priv->suspend_count++                                          :1139
  │    i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv)                             :1143
  │
  └─ display (NOT dev_priv) is the only thing handed to the display layer:
       intel_power_domains_disable(display)                              :1112
       intel_display_driver_suspend(display)   ◀── the target call        :1120
       intel_hpd_cancel_work(display), intel_encoder_suspend_all(display),
       intel_dpt_suspend(display), i9xx_display_sr_save(display),
       intel_opregion_suspend(display, opregion_target_state), intel_dmc_suspend(display)

intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)   intel_display_driver.c:684
  ├─ HAS_DISPLAY(display)                     -> early return 0
  ├─ display->drm            -> drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)   :692
  ├─ display->restore.modeset_state = state   (saved for resume)          :697
  ├─ display->wq.cleanup     -> flush_workqueue()  (unpins DPT VMAs)      :700
  └─ intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)                                        :702
```

Summary of the flow: `struct device *kdev` → `drm_device *` → `drm_i915_private *dev_priv` → **narrowed to `dev_priv->display`** at `i915_driver.c:1106`. `intel_display_driver_suspend` never sees `dev_priv`; it reaches the DRM device again via `display->drm`. That narrowing is deliberate — it's the ongoing effort to decouple `display/` from `drm_i915_private` so the display code can be shared with Xe. `display->restore.modeset_state` is the one piece of state that outlives the call, consumed on resume by `__intel_display_driver_resume` (`:708`).
